authority_guard: Hebrew forms, lemmas, roots, morphology, Strong's tags, English formatting, variants, canonical reuse, Second Temple evidence, and rabbinic reception are contextual evidence only, never automatic meaning, boundary authority, theology, preferred-reading authority, or graph authority.

findings.issue: Gen.25.1-11 combines a Keturah descendant/inheritance register with Abraham's death-burial summary and Isaac transition despite a discourse-function change at 25:7.
findings.proposed_boundary_or_remedy: Prefer Gen.25.1-6 and Gen.25.7-11; if retained as a parent, register both as mandatory internal units.
findings.Hebrew_or_translation_reason: 25:7 shifts to a summative life formula, death and burial; 25:11 transfers focus to Isaac. Form and discourse converge on a seam.

findings.issue: Gen.26.1-33 is defensible as a parent but its rationale under-reports three internal scene/function seams.
findings.proposed_boundary_or_remedy: Retain parent if desired; explicitly register Gen.26.1-11, 26.12-25, and 26.26-33 as internal units.
findings.Hebrew_or_translation_reason: Participant configuration and narrative function change at 26:12, 26:23, and 26:26 while Hebrew clause chains preserve cycle continuity.

findings.issue: The rationale attaches 26:34-35 to the blessing conflict without acknowledging its stronger lexical/thematic frame with 27:46-28:9.
findings.proposed_boundary_or_remedy: Keep current seam only with an explicit anticipatory-frame note; alternatively consider a Gen.26.34-28.9 parent with internal scenes.
findings.Hebrew_or_translation_reason: The wife-grief notice at 26:34-35 is resumed at 27:46 and motivates the commission and Esau's responsive marriage.

findings.issue: Gen.33:18-20 changes from reunion/separation itinerary to a new Shechem arrival, land-acquisition, and altar scene.
findings.Hebrew_or_translation_reason: 33:16 closes Esau's departure, 33:17 gives Jacob's Succoth movement, and 33:18 begins a new arrival, location, encampment, purchase, and altar. The translation difficulty of shalem does not create the seam; discourse does.

findings.issue: Gen.35.16-29 combines several completed notices with changing participant focus and function.
findings.proposed_boundary_or_remedy: Prefer Gen.35.16-20, 35.21-26, and 35.27-29; retain an optional parent transition group only if hierarchy is supported.
findings.Hebrew_or_translation_reason: Travel and Rachel's death begin at 35:16; a new Israel journey, Reuben notice, and son register begin at 35:21; arrival to Isaac and Isaac's death begin at 35:27.

premortem_failures: Shared-error consensus may preserve over-large units.
Editorial markers may be mistaken for ancient divisions.
Toledot, wayyiqtol, roots, or lemma transitions may become mechanical rules.
Glosses or etymologies may replace contextual meaning.
Variant-sensitive wording may silently select a reading.
Later canonical reuse may be reverse-engineered into Genesis boundaries.
Second Temple and later rabbinic layers may be collapsed.
Genesis 6:1-4 may be isolated so that a debated interpretation gains authority.
Unreviewed child spans may bypass parent review.
Canonical cross-references may become automatic graph edges.
